Schema-v3 validation reports record non-sensitive provider, policy-mode, support-level, explicit/implicit selection, access-rule counts, and rule_kind/rule_index provenance. They do not prove Docker confinement, identity injection, restart recovery, backup restore, join correctness, links, or per-user reachability.

For Headscale, v0.1.0-rc.1 failed the first live TrueNAS network-attachment gate and was rolled back safely; v0.1.0-rc.2 corrects that topology but has not yet passed end-to-end acceptance. For Tailscale SaaS, recorded 2026-10-08 checks confirmed HTTP 200 with no-store/identity Vary and healthy /healthz, but did not independently capture a running-container digest. Published RC.17 shared editing and the RC.18 browser-local extension must not be conflated. A plain browser-URL GET returned a page titled qBittorrent WebUI; this was not a backend probe, proof of login, or a diagnosis of an earlier Unauthorized response. Token refresh/revocation, separate owner mapping, unsupported HTTP-policy and SSH-suppression cases, two-identity service/machine isolation, copied-target parity, HTTP/SSH reachability, and live hostname-proposal acceptance remain unaccepted.

No public support claim is warranted until the selected provider's live checklist plus at least two real identities, LAN-negative Velociportal access, restart persistence, every NPM join, every card link, and actual control-plane reachability have been checked. Use the real-deployment worksheet.

docs.title: Service-hosted MCP (RC.20 candidate)
docs.text:
The current source adds an opt-in /mcp endpoint in the existing Velociportal service, for finite icons, the caller's durable personal entries, and shared presentation icons and default card order on already-authorized cards. No workstation hosts a second server. There is no model, upstream administration, login system, token issuer, database, or new listener.

RC.20 candidate, not verified deployment or universal client support

v0.2.0-rc.20 is the selected prerelease candidate for MCP, durable personal storage and metadata v4. Immutable RC.18/19 do not contain these features; RC.19 fixes the earlier route panic. This preparation does not assert an RC.20 image/digest has been published. Use these opt-ins only with a verified compatible immutable image and separately approved storage/deployment. On 2026-11-14 the owner authorized prerelease publication with the remaining native-client and live-acceptance gaps disclosed, rather than blocking publication. This is not a compatibility, security, deployment or support certification; it authorizes no live NAS, storage, permissions, network or Serve changes. Tailscale remains preview.

docs.title: Client status and endpoint boundary
docs.text:
Claude Code 2.1.321 passed 12 native HTTP tool calls across two fresh processes (14 internal turns) against the production handler on localhost with synthetic identity: finite icons, durable personal create/read/delete, NPM shared-icon set/reset, and reconnect/read of initialized-empty state. This was not a server restart or genuine Serve test. personal_update and Machine/Application native target or mutation calls were not exercised. Native Codex CLI was unavailable; native T3 had no supported temporary enrollment path and remains unverified. Genuine Serve/two-device identity, native browser, live restart/recovery, LAN-negative and the full provider acceptance matrix remain unverified. Compatibility with one CLI does not establish another client's integration. T3 still needs its actual connection path tested, including whether it connects itself or through a provider integration.

The intended endpoint is the existing portal origin plus /mcp, for example the illustrative http://portal.tailnet.ts.net:8081/mcp. This is not a deployed address or working client setup. The canonical path remains tailnet-only HTTP Serve :8081 -> http://127.0.0.1:18080; WireGuard protects ordinary on-path traffic. Plain HTTP is not HTTPS or a browser secure context. Endpoint/control-plane/host compromise remains in scope.

A client must support this non-localhost plain-HTTP path, stateless JSON responses, the protocol/header rules below, and genuine human Serve identity. A cloud connector, tagged machine, unsupported OAuth requirement, HTTPS-only client restriction, or unsupported transport is an incompatibility to report—not permission to add tokens, a trust-wrapper bypass, identity relay, workstation server, public tunnel, SSO, or new Serve/TLS infrastructure. No client installation/enrollment command is offered as verified setup.

docs.title: Opt-in configuration
docs.text:
Variable Exact source behavior PORTAL_MCP_ORIGIN Absent disables /mcp (404). Supplied empty/invalid fails configuration. Canonical HTTP(S) origin only; must equal every enabled shared/personal origin. PORTAL_PERSONAL_SERVICES_ORIGIN Independent Tailscale-only personal catalog opt-in; absent disables. Must be the existing portal origin, not an application URL. PORTAL_PERSONAL_SERVICES_FILE Absent retains browser-managed volatile RAM mode. Present requires Tailscale, personal origin, valid namespace and preexisting valid private storage. Personal MCP tools require this durable mode. PORTAL_STATE_NAMESPACE Canonical [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63} source binding. Required for durable storage and every v4 reader/writer; supplied empty/invalid always fails. Requires a metadata file or private file consumer, not merely MCP. PORTAL_EDIT_MODE=shared, PORTAL_EDITORS, PORTAL_PUBLIC_ORIGIN, SERVICE_METADATA_FILE Existing shared-editor prerequisites remain necessary for shared target/icon tools; add a valid namespace. Exact editor allowlist, not automatic administrator-role permission. PORTAL_CUSTOM_ICONS Unreleased source only. Absent keeps everything below unchanged. Exactly enabled adds three custom PNG logo tools and requires shared editing, PORTAL_MCP_ORIGIN and a namespace. Writes metadata v5.

MCP alone creates neither a personal store nor a shared writer/lock and does not change edit mode. Readonly/off/browser metadata can render v4 defaults without enabling shared tools. RAM personal entries can supply the editor's own active application target for shared icon operations, but cannot be read or mutated through personal MCP tools. Headscale has finite icons and eligible NPM shared targets only; it gains no personal or SSH Machine support. The generic shared tool schema may still list machine/application kinds: Headscale Machine listing is empty; Application without a personal store is unavailable as not_found.

Use storage and recovery and the opt-in deployment checkpoint before configuring files. All values remain disabled/commented in the examples. Production provider env files retain go-quoted-v1 values through Compose raw env-file forwarding; origin/file/namespace values are quoted there, not shell-evaluated.

docs.title: Identity on every request
docs.text:
IdentityMiddleware accepts Tailscale-User-* only from TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDR. MCP additionally requires an exact canonical unpadded full human login, consistent singleton identity headers, and exact configured Host. Initialization, clientInfo, arguments, prior discovery, handles and RPC IDs never select an identity or retain permission. Each operation rechecks the actual request, current configuration, fresh complete snapshot and current target/owner, including at the final pre-rename checkpoint.

Human-device authority is shared by processes on that device. It is not independent agent authentication or a sandbox against another process using the same human's network authority. Tagged/no-human-identity, Funnel and cloud-connector impersonation are unsupported. The host-loopback trusted-workload boundary also remains: host processes that can reach the raw loopback socket may share the trusted source. Do not widen the trusted CIDR or expose that socket.

Admission Accepted headers Native Origin and all Fetch Metadata absent Same-origin browser-shaped request Exactly one matching Origin; any supplied Sec-Fetch-Site must be same-origin, Sec-Fetch-Mode must be cors or same-origin, and Sec-Fetch-Dest must be empty Always rejected Sec-Fetch-User; empty/null/duplicate/cross-origin Origin; Fetch Metadata without Origin or contradictory values; Authorization, Cookie, Mcp-Session-Id, preflight request headers—even empty

There is no permissive CORS or alternative bearer/cookie/session authentication. Browser personal/shared APIs keep their own exact Origin/Host and CSRF rules; MCP is a separate guarded transport, not a CSRF bypass to browser endpoints.

docs.title: Wire contract and resource bounds
docs.text:
• Exact /mcp, POST only after admission. Enabled unsupported methods return 405; no GET event stream. Query/ForceQuery, encoded paths and trailing-slash aliases are unsupported.
  • One JSON-RPC 2.0 object; no batches. Content-Type: application/json (optional UTF-8 charset), and one Accept header advertising both application/json and text/event-stream without media parameters. Responses choose JSON, not SSE.
  • Only protocol 2025-11-25 is implemented. initialize may omit MCP-Protocol-Version; supplied versions must match. Initialization returns the supported version, which the client must accept before proceeding. Subsequent calls require the matching header. The historical serverInfo name velociportal-readonly-prototype and version 0.1.0 are compatibility labels, not the application release version or a statement that writes are impossible.
  • Methods: initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call. Valid admitted notifications return 202 without executing application reads/mutations; notification-shaped tool calls are not saves. No sessions, legacy SSE, server push, tasks, sampling, subscriptions or bulk import.
  • Eight immediately admitted MCP requests; excess returns 503, not an unbounded queue. Personal reads/mutations also acquire one of the same eight personal slots shared with browser requests, not eight additional personal slots. Slots remain held through synchronous dispatch/commit.
  • 16 KiB complete request, JSON depth 16, route-local read/write deadline 10 seconds, and 256 KiB complete response, including RPC envelope/ID and both structuredContent and text representations. No truncated success. JSON rejects unknown, duplicate, case-variant and null fields where not explicitly permitted; tool objects have exact allowed keys. Encoding failure after a successful mutation is uncertain, not rollback.
  • Identity-derived responses are no-store. Tool arguments, private URLs, ownership IDs and result bodies must not be logged. Client-side transcripts may contain the caller's authored data: treat them as private too.

docs.title: The ten fixed tools
docs.text:
Discovery is recomputed per request and may advertise fewer tools when storage/ownership/freshness/editor capability is unavailable. Dispatch repeats authority checks even if the client retained a descriptor.

Tool Arguments Result / authority icons_list Empty object Finite embedded icon IDs and labels; no private catalog or network fetch personal_read Empty object Own confirmed durable state and coarse per-entry projection; fresh exact-login + Users API ID ownership personal_create store_id, generation, revision, name, url; optional icon Own confirmed state after create; omitted icon means inherit personal_update Create fields plus own id Replace that own entry's authored fields; omitted icon clears the authored override to inherit personal_delete store_id, generation, revision, own id Own confirmed state after delete; initialized-empty remains authoritative shared_targets_list kind; optional cursor, limit Current caller-visible targets of one kind: npm, machine, or application shared_target_get target exactly {kind, handle} Selected name/shared/effective icon, NPM category/order when set, and opaque revision, target_revision shared_icon_set target, revision, target_revision, finite nonempty icon {"status":"saved"} only after confirmed shared commit shared_icon_reset target, revision, target_revision Remove only selected shared icon/default; same confirmed-save result shared_order_set revision, entries (1–64 distinct NPM targets) Set or remove shared default category/order in one commit; {"status":"saved","revision":"…"}

Personal results contain own authored document, durable, stable store_id, process generation, collection revision, initialized state and coarse projection—not a whole private file, browser CSRF token, foreign collection or policy snapshot. There is no MCP restore/import tool. No tool accepts an arbitrary shared destination URL/path/digest/provider-ID tuple. Icons are finite embedded IDs, never uploads, external logos or filesystem paths.

Shared target selection uses actual current card evidence: policy-matched NPM service; full supported SSH + independent Grant TCP/22 + current device capability for a Machine; or the maintainer's own active personal entry for an application. It never enumerates foreign personal records, the global digest map, matching-user counts or backend topology. No icon creates a card or supplies authorization.

docs.title: Shared default card order
docs.text:
shared_targets_list and shared_target_get include an NPM target's current shared category (string) and order (integer 0–1,000,000) when the shared file sets them; absent fields are omitted. Machine and application summaries never carry them.

shared_order_set takes the shared document revision from either read tool and entries, an array of 1–64 objects. Each entry has exactly target plus at least one of order and category:

{"revision": "…", "entries": [
  {"target": {"kind": "npm", "handle": "…"}, "order": 10, "category": "Media"},
  {"target": {"kind": "npm", "handle": "…"}, "order": null}
]}
  • A value sets the field, null removes it, and an omitted field is left unchanged. A touched entry left with no fields is removed from the file.
  • Every target must be a distinct, currently visible NPM service for the caller. Duplicate targets are invalid arguments. A machine, application, missing or invisible target returns the unavailable-target response (not_found) and nothing is written.
  • All entries are applied in one commit with whole-document CAS, or none are. Every target is rechecked immediately before the rename. A stale revision returns conflict. Setting values that are already current returns the current revision without writing.
  • The result carries the new document revision, so a client can chain another call without re-reading. Lost or uncertain responses still require read-back, not replay.
  • The writer is the ordinary lossless NPM writer: a legacy file becomes v3, v4 stays v4 and v5 stays v5. Name, link, icon, custom icon, other entries, machine/application arrays, binding and null presence are preserved.
  • It requires the same shared-editor capability as the icon tools. It changes presentation order only: it never creates, hides or authorizes a card.
  • Sixty-four entries with 64-character ASCII categories fit the 16 KiB request limit; long non-ASCII categories may need smaller batches.

This sets the shared default order everyone sees. A personal order saved in a browser (Account settings → Edit card order) still applies on top of it in that browser.

docs.title: Opt-in custom PNG logo tools (unreleased source)
docs.text:
With PORTAL_CUSTOM_ICONS=enabled, discovery appends three tools after the shared tools, under the same shared-editor capability. With it absent, discovery and calls are unchanged and these names are unknown tools (-32602).

Tool Arguments Result / authority custom_icon_import png_base64 (standard padded base64, at most 10,924 characters), revision {"status":"saved","custom_icon":"sha256:…"}. Stores one canonical re-encoded PNG. Identical images return the same ID without writing. Assigns nothing. custom_icon_get target exactly {kind, handle}; NPM only Name, current custom_icon (empty when none), opaque revision and target_revision custom_icon_set target, revision, target_revision, custom_icon (stored ID, or empty to clear) {"status":"saved"} after a confirmed shared commit; an unchanged assignment does not write

Machine and application targets return the unavailable-target response. There is no listing of stored images, gallery, delete or cleanup tool. The image renders only inside markup for authorized cards. Formats, limits, versioning and downgrade: custom PNG logos.

docs.title: Pages and optimistic concurrency
docs.text:
Target pages contain at most 64 entries (default 64; supplied integer 1–64), may be shorter to meet the full response byte budget, and have no total count. Handles are caller/provider/namespace/kind/process bound. The opaque cursor is also caller/kind/source/process bound (current encoding 87 bytes, bounded at 256); every page recomputes current authorization. It is not a frozen catalog: if the anchor disappears, the call conflicts and the client must restart listing; new earlier-sorting handles may require a fresh listing to see them.

Shared saves compare the complete shared-file byte revision and current target revision. Any intervening shared save can conflict, even in another target kind. Personal mutations compare stable store ID, fresh process generation and own collection revision; no whole-private-file revision discloses other users' activity. Never refresh CAS silently, auto-merge, retry a mutation or treat the JSON-RPC ID as an idempotency key.

docs.title: Failure and recovery
docs.text:
Invalid arguments or unknown tool names return protocol -32602 (Invalid params). Operation failures return coarse isError:true results with error such as forbidden, not_found, unavailable, conflict, uncertain, capacity, or invalid_request, without parser/filesystem detail. Missing/invisible/foreign/inactive/unsupported-ID targets share the unavailable-target response; current authority is established before exposing a CAS conflict.

A timeout, cancellation, disconnected response or uncertain encoding after commit does not mean rollback. Read back confirmed state and review; never replay automatically. If private storage is uncertain, both adapters suppress authoritative private reads and writes until validated locked reopen/reconciliation. Shared uncertainty disables shared mutations and editable read-back; older confirmed presentation may still decorate visible cards but is not proof a save failed. These failure domains are independent: private failure does not disable NPM/Machine shared operations. See offline recovery and downgrade.

Current ownership/visibility comes from the latest complete snapshot, with the three-poll-interval freshness cutoff. Polling delay and the final-check-to-rename interval remain a bounded stale-evidence/revocation window, not transactional upstream revocation or an enforcement guarantee. Network/config changes and filesystem sync do not erase that window.

docs.title: Remaining client and live acceptance worksheet
docs.text:
These checks remain unverified acceptance requirements, not completed product tests. The owner waived them as prepublication blockers for RC.20 only; no live work is authorized by that waiver. Retain the complete TrueNAS provider worksheet and real-deployment validation. The scoped localhost native-Claude result above does not complete this worksheet.

  • [ ] Record a future published immutable image digest containing this exact source feature set; retain RC.18/19 unchanged. Record runtime UID/GID, exact independent directories/files, modes, source namespace, backup and downgrade plan before owner approval.
  • [ ] For installed native Claude Code, Codex CLI and T3 Code, record exact versions and actual connector origin. Prove initialize, discovery, real bounded tool call, reconnect and JSON responses on the intended transport—not a direct HTTP substitute for a native call.
  • [ ] Use two human-owned Tailscale machines with no workstation acting as server. Prove same-human authored state across devices and a second distinct human's isolation. Prove genuine Serve header injection/replacement and reject tagged/no-human, alternate-auth and direct raw-source requests. Raw port must be unreachable from the LAN.
  • [ ] Compare current NPM, personal application and full triple-evidence Machine cards with actual HTTP/SSH reachability for both identities. Test all three icon kinds, explicit generic versus inherit, reset, browser/shared preservation, rename versus replacement and namespace/source mismatch.
  • [ ] Remove editor permission, owner/direct membership or relevant Grant/SSH/capability evidence while retaining old descriptors/handles/revisions. Once current evidence reflects removal, reads/writes must fail as specified; record polling/revocation delay, not instantaneous enforcement.
  • [ ] Confirm an acknowledged durable save, close all browsers, restart the deployment and then reconnect. Disk is authoritative after a fresh complete owner snapshot; cold/stale ownership reveals no private data, initialized-empty stays empty, old generations conflict and no browser restore is required.
  • [ ] In a controlled separately approved recovery environment, exercise missing/corrupt/wrong-permission storage, wrong namespace/owner ID, conflicting browser drafts/backups, uncertain response reconciliation and private offline backup/restore. Never inject failures into production merely to complete this checklist.
  • [ ] Native browser keyboard/focus/touch, unsaved drafts, conflicting legacy copies, explicit restore-only-into-absent behavior and two-device changes pass. Synthetic DOM tests are not this proof.
  • [ ] Complete live OAuth refresh/revocation, authoritative role and separate owner mapping, unsupported HTTP-policy/SSH negatives, stale/cold recovery, copied-target parity, Serve restart/header replacement and LAN-negative checks before any Tailscale support promotion.

The recorded S5 suite and independent static review establish source behavior with synthetic requests/snapshots and owned temporary files. They do not certify native clients, real Serve identity, distributed synchronization, live restart, filesystem disaster recovery or production security.

docs.title: Nginx Proxy Manager API
docs.text: Velociportal uses Nginx Proxy Manager (NPM) as its current service catalog.

docs.title: Runtime calls
docs.text:
1. POST /api/tokens with identity and secret to obtain a JWT.
  2. GET /api/nginx/proxy-hosts with that Bearer token.
  3. On 401, authenticate once more and retry the request.

The current polling cache does not fetch access lists.

docs.title: Proxy-host fields used
docs.text:
{
  "id": 12,
  "domain_names": ["grafana.example.com"],
  "forward_scheme": "http",
  "forward_host": "10.0.0.20",
  "forward_port": 3000,
  "access_list_id": 3,
  "enabled": true,
  "meta": { "nginx_online": true }
}
  • enabled and the presence of at least one domain determine whether the record can become a card.
  • The first valid concrete domain_names entry becomes the automatic card name and URL host. A wildcard may appear earlier without taking precedence.
  • A wildcard-only host remains visible after policy matching but is non-clickable until it has a concrete NPM name or an explicit service-metadata URL.
  • Adding the real concrete hostname to the same NPM proxy host is the preferred correction because NPM then remains the browser-name source of truth. Creating a duplicate proxy host can create duplicate cards.
  • forward_scheme becomes the automatic card URL scheme after an HTTP/HTTPS allowlist check. Exact-ID service metadata may override only presentation fields: browser target/display name in v1, plus category/order in v2.
  • forward_host is the current access-rule destination join key.
  • forward_port is required for exact TCP capability matching when a Tailscale Grant supplies card evidence. Legacy ACL ports remain unmodeled.
  • For an explicitly configured health target, forward_scheme, forward_host, and forward_port also define the direct backend probe target. Presentation-metadata URLs never participate.
  • meta.nginx_online is retained only as NPM route/configuration state in diagnostics. It is not backend application health and never creates a health label.
  • access_list_id is parsed but not used in visibility matching.

docs.title: Optional presentation metadata
docs.text:
A strict versioned JSON file can override the displayed name or browser URL for an existing NPM proxy-host ID. Metadata is applied only after policy matching and cannot create a card, enable a host, change forward_host/forward_port, or grant visibility. Unknown IDs produce only a count in diagnostics.

Source priority is:

  1. A concrete hostname on the existing NPM proxy host.
  2. An explicit operator metadata URL/name when NPM cannot represent the desired browser target.
  3. Future DNS/Tailscale observations as non-authoritative suggestions only.

Velociportal never invents a wildcard-derived URL.

docs.title: Access-list endpoint
docs.text: The client still contains a GET /api/nginx/access-lists helper, but the runtime cache and matcher do not call or use it. NPM access lists remain an independent enforcement/configuration layer.

docs.title: Transport security
docs.text:
NPM authentication sends a reusable password. Plain HTTP is accepted only for the exact canonical private Docker alias or same-host/loopback compatibility routes; production uses http://npm.velociportal.internal:81 on velociportal-upstreams. Use HTTPS with a valid certificate for every other location.

No scoped Velociportal token

NPM uses user credential login rather than a purpose-built read-only API key. Use a dedicated account with the least permissions that still permit proxy-host listing, protect the password, and verify its effective privileges in your NPM version.

docs.title: Service metadata and editing
docs.text:
RC.20 candidate versus earlier releases. RC.18 introduced browser-local editing and the personal RAM catalog but has an optional-API startup panic. Immutable RC.19 contains the route correction at a7fd76d807c6a5d608a09634409c1b9cf322edf7; neither contains MCP, durable personal storage or metadata v4. These opt-ins are selected for v0.2.0-rc.20, without asserting a published image/digest or live enablement. Remaining client/live gaps are disclosed, not RC.20 prepublication blockers. Tailscale remains preview; separate deployment, storage and migration approval is still required.

Presentation never changes policy, NPM, DNS, backend targets, SSH evidence or access. The published RAM-only behavior remains the source default when no private file is configured. See MCP transport/tools and remaining acceptance.

docs.title: Policy first, server defaults
docs.text:
SERVICE_METADATA_FILE is the optional server presentation configuration source. Entries associate with existing positive NPM proxy_host_id values after supported policy matching. Metadata cannot create, hide or enable cards, repair a domainless host, or alter health. A concrete NPM domain remains the preferred default; a wildcard-only card remains visible without a usable link until an explicit URL is supplied.

The strict reader accepts:

Version Fields in each service entry 1 proxy_host_id, optional name and url 2 v1 plus optional category and order 3 (RC.17) v2 plus optional finite icon ID 4 (RC.20 candidate) Existing NPM fields plus required source binding and separate Machine/application icon arrays; see the v4 contract below

Legacy v1–v3 documents require exact version and services keys. Unknown, duplicate, case-variant, malformed and trailing JSON is rejected. The complete file is bounded to 256 KiB and 1,024 entries. Names are canonical unpadded strings up to 120 Unicode code points; URLs are bounded to 2,048 bytes and must be validated absolute HTTP(S) URLs without credentials or wildcard hosts. Categories are canonical strings up to 64 characters; order is an integer from 0 through 1,000,000. Existing v1/v2 name/url null presence remains readable and is preserved for untouched entries. Category and order require v2, v3 or v4; icons require v3 or v4.

{
  "version": 3,
  "services": [
    {
      "proxy_host_id": 7,
      "name": "Media",
      "url": "https://media.example.com",
      "category": "Home",
      "order": 10,
      "icon": "jellyfin"
    }
  ]
}

Categories and order group/sort only authorized cards, with uncategorized last and deterministic name/ID fallbacks. The dashboard edits only name, URL and icon. Neither editing mode changes category/order, health targets, SSH or the authorized card set. A shared editor can change the shared default category/order of visible NPM cards through the MCP shared_order_set tool; it uses the same shared writer and never changes which cards anyone can see. Startup does not write or migrate metadata. suggest-hostnames emits a strict v1 proposal fragment; never replace a complete v2/v3 file with that fragment. Preserve category/order/icons and unrelated entries when reviewing an operator merge.

docs.title: Personal card order
docs.text: In Account settings → Edit card order, drag a grip or use the up/down buttons, then Save order. This changes only the order of visible services within their existing groups, not the shared metadata or anyone else's view. New services follow the ordered ones. Use default order → Save order returns to the server's current order. The setting stores only service IDs in this browser for this identity; it does not record clicks, sync across devices, or affect Machines. A personal order may override the shared default order in that browser.

docs.title: Editing mode selection (RC.18)
docs.text:
PORTAL_EDIT_MODE accepts only canonical lowercase off, browser, or shared. Explicit empty, padded, case-variant and unknown values fail configuration.

Setting Result Absent Preserve RC.17 exactly: both shared settings absent disables editing; supplied settings follow existing shared validation, including failure for partial/invalid values off No editor controls, writer initialization or edit API; retained shared settings are ignored, not deleted; normal readonly metadata still loads browser Personal presentation for any trusted viewer's currently authorized cards; no allowlist, public origin, metadata file or writable mount required shared Require exact editor logins, canonical public origin and the existing safe single-file writer storage

Browser mode rejects supplied PORTAL_EDITORS or PORTAL_PUBLIC_ORIGIN, even empty values. Ordinary readonly SERVICE_METADATA_FILE is allowed as the source of browser defaults. With an independently verified corrected RC.19-or-newer image and separate deployment approval, add the single line PORTAL_EDIT_MODE: browser to the existing Compose service's environment mapping; no editor directory overlay is needed. Production provider env files may instead use PORTAL_EDIT_MODE="browser" with their existing go-quoted-v1 convention. RC.17 itself does not implement this selector or personal editing.

docs.title: Browser-local interaction and persistence (RC.18)
docs.text:
The existing Edit dialog uses Save, Cancel, Reset, and quiet “Saved in this browser” help. No mode switch or dashboard banner is added. Empty fields remove only that field's local override. Reset removes this service's local name/link/icon choices and restores the current server-rendered defaults, including optional metadata, not necessarily raw NPM values. It never modifies the server file or anyone else's browser.

The browser stores only user-entered name/URL/finite-icon overrides in a versioned map by canonical positive service ID: at most 1,024 entries and 256 KiB serialized UTF-8. Its key uses the existing opaque SHA-256 digest of the exact login, never the raw login. Browser origin supplies deployment separation. There is no cross-device or cross-browser persistence, account synchronization or server backup. Clearing site storage removes these choices; private windows and blocked/cleared storage may have none. Logo and SSH-account suggestions remain separate browser-local preferences.

Loaded data and saves are both untrusted and validated: exact field types/allowed fields, positive safe-integer IDs, 120-code-point names, 2,048-byte HTTP(S) URLs without userinfo/controls/padding, and finite icon choices. The browser deliberately rejects ambiguous WHATWG normalization such as shorthand IPs, host-case/default-port rewrites and dot segments; it is a conservative subset, not an assertion that Go and browser URL parsers are identical. Names update as text, icon paths come only from the fixed rendered registry, and link updates use safe DOM operations rather than stored HTML.

Only current authorized DOM cards receive preferences. Stored IDs never create cards or reveal missing topology; absent-card preferences may remain inert within the bounds. Positive NPM ID reuse can inherit old presentation, never authorization: reset/remove obsolete choices when IDs are repurposed. The browser stores no catalog, policy, access decisions, credentials or shared form tokens and makes zero edit API calls. Normal server polling still updates authorization.

Each fresh fragment supplies new immutable server defaults, then local preferences are applied and search is recomputed. Personal URLs update visible/search domains and linked/unlinked navigation without affecting probes. Local names do not reorder server categories or cards. Drafts survive harmless polling/search filtering; search-hidden is not unauthorized. Identity, mode or editing-availability changes invalidate the controller and require a full reload; loss of the current service clears its draft. Same-origin cross-tab events do not replace dirty forms, and saves reread the current validated map to preserve unrelated entries. Simultaneous writes are not transactional or promised conflict-free.

Unavailable, full or corrupt storage does not break browsing. Failed saves keep the draft and state not saved, never claim persistence or silently overwrite corrupt data. Browser blank/reset still requires working, valid storage; operator-cleared site storage restores defaults but also removes other preferences at that origin. Synthetic DOM/controller fixtures do not prove native dialog focus, layout, keyboard/touch or live behavior.

docs.title: Personal tailnet services (RC.18)
docs.text: Personal entries are separate from NPM presentation metadata and browser-local overrides. They support ordinary Tailscale-native HTTPS applications without an NPM host, but do not remove the selected-provider-plus-NPM dependency, alter /healthz, or administer upstreams. RC.17 includes neither this catalog nor browser mode.

docs.title: Enablement and use
docs.text:
PORTAL_PERSONAL_SERVICES_ORIGIN is an independent opt-in, available only with CONTROL_PLANE=tailscale. Its value must be the exact canonical HTTP(S) origin already used to open this portal: for example, the placeholder http://portal.tailnet.ts.net:8081, without a path, query, fragment or trailing slash. Absence disables store/routes/controls; supplied empty/invalid values or Headscale fail configuration. It is not an application destination, a new listener or an instruction to change Serve/DNS/TLS. An independently verified corrected RC.19-or-newer image and a separately approved deployment change are needed; no live configuration is performed here.

No file, database, writable mount, extra container, PORTAL_EDITORS or shared writer is needed. PORTAL_EDIT_MODE still independently selects NPM presentation editing: off does not disable an explicitly enabled personal catalog, and browser still never sends NPM edit requests. Shared mode retains its existing allowlist/origin/storage guards.

Use Add service near Services for a name, normal launch link and optional finite embedded icon. Personal cards have their own Edit action; Your services in account settings also manages edit/delete and recovery, including saved entries not currently displayed. Inactive entries have coarse status and no clickable bypass link. Creation/editing/recovery require JavaScript; eligible server-rendered links already in RAM remain usable without it. Personal IDs are opaque and separate from positive NPM IDs; NPM metadata, category/order, health and shared-edit APIs do not join to them.

docs.title: Links and current policy evidence
docs.text:
Links are canonical HTTPS URLs to a current device's canonical *.ts.net hostname, with an optional validated nondefault port and application path. Names are bounded to 120 Unicode code points and links to 2,048 bytes. IP fallbacks, arbitrary domains, userinfo, queries, fragments, controls, padding and unsafe normalization are rejected. Never save pairing URLs, pairing codes or other secrets. Query/fragment exclusion rejects common pairing-link forms but cannot detect every secret someone might embed in a path; use the normal launch address, and let the app handle its own pairing/sign-in.

Every render resolves that hostname to exactly one current normalized device and requires a positive network Grant permitting TCP to the link's ingress port (443 by default), for the exact authoritative direct member's supported login/group/role evidence. Legacy ACLs are not port evidence. Device ownership, tags on a person's devices, SSH policy/capability and NPM are not substitutes. Hostname binding follows the current device with that exact name, including a replacement that acquires it; missing, renamed, malformed or ambiguous names suppress the active card. Cold, future-dated or stale complete-snapshot evidence (older than three polling intervals) suppresses personal cards without changing existing NPM stale-render behavior. Authored inactive records remain manageable. A card is not enforcement, a health check, a reachability guarantee or proof of application login.

docs.title: Volatile availability, conflicts and explicit recovery
docs.text:
The existing process retains at most 128 initialized collections, including initialized-empty collections; each versioned document allows 128 entries and 64 KiB canonical serialized data. GET does not allocate collections. Capacity exhaustion fails explicitly rather than silently evicting another user's latest catalog. Collections are private to the same exact trusted login, not shared with other tailnet users. They are not encrypted from the trusted server/host operator.

During that process lifetime, same-login devices can read the latest acknowledged catalog without another browser being online. Existing portal polling announces generation/revision changes; there is no separate sync service or polling subsystem. Each mutation compares process generation and collection revision atomically. A concurrent change conflicts: preserve the draft, reload/review, and save deliberately. There is no automatic overwrite, merge, last-arrival-wins, offline commit queue or automatic mutation retry. A timeout after POST is uncertain; the controller reads back state to reconcile rather than blindly repeating the write.

Each browser may retain the latest confirmed authored document plus format/generation/revision under the opaque exact-login digest and origin. Load/save validates untrusted data and guards storage errors. No raw login, CSRF/session token, policy, device topology, rendered card catalog or authorization decisions are stored. This is an explicit authored-data recovery copy, not a PWA/authorization cache. NPM browser-local overrides, logo and SSH-account preferences remain separate and unsynchronized. A server save can succeed while browser backup fails; the UI distinguishes those outcomes.

Restart/redeploy loses the server RAM catalog. An absent server collection never automatically uploads or erases a retained browser copy. Restore from this browser requires explicit action and the same revision/generation guard; a competing create/restore conflicts. A prior-generation copy remains until explicit restore or adoption of the current server collection. A browser's copy may be stale: Velociportal cannot prove it is newest. If all copies are lost, recovery is impossible. Deleting every entry leaves initialized-empty authoritative state, which must not resurrect old entries from a recovery copy.

This file-absent volatile mode provides no crash durability or personal MCP tools. Optional durable source behavior is described below. History, a backup service, account-synchronized NPM preferences, iroh, CRDT and a generic bookmark/plugin framework remain absent. Synthetic controller/server fixtures do not establish native layout/focus/keyboard/touch or real two-device/restart acceptance; those remain separate pending checks.

docs.title: Optional exact-login shared editors (RC.17)
docs.text:
Shared mode retains the existing guards. Both settings absent keep RC.17 read-only behavior; partial configuration fails. Both present require an existing valid SERVICE_METADATA_FILE in safe, separately provisioned writable storage.

Setting Contract PORTAL_EDITORS Strict JSON array, at most 32 exact full logins, each at most 254 bytes; no padding, controls, duplicates, aliases, case folding or inferred roles PORTAL_PUBLIC_ORIGIN Exact canonical browser-facing HTTP(S) origin, including non-default port when used; no path, query, fragment, userinfo, wildcard or trailing slash

An empty editor array configures storage but grants nobody editing. RC.17 disables editing by removing both settings, not empty strings. The RC.18 selector additionally allows explicit off without deleting retained settings. Tailnet HTTP Serve remains supported; no HTTPS infrastructure change is implied.

The narrow setup subcommand validates these settings, preserving other environment entries:

velociportal setup service-editor --env-file velociportal.env --editors '["alice@example.com"]' --origin http://portal.tailnet.ts.net:8081

In the RC.18 extension setup also sets PORTAL_EDIT_MODE=shared. SERVICE_METADATA_FILE must already be set; when Compose supplies it, use the corresponding fixed runtime path in the operator configuration too. Setup never provisions or probes metadata storage. Logins in arguments can be visible to trusted same-host administration tools/history; authenticated private env editing is an alternative. Disable without changing metadata:

velociportal setup service-editor --env-file velociportal.env --disable

The RC.18 disable path removes both shared keys and sets PORTAL_EDIT_MODE=off. Doctor reports browser-local mode without writer/storage inspection, or coarse shared read-only prerequisites. It creates no editor lock/probe files, performs no write test and prints no editor identities/origin or saved URLs in that diagnostic. Passing is not lifetime-lock, durability or save proof. Other Doctor upstream checks remain networked.

Only configured exact logins receive shared Edit buttons, including wildcard cards. Ordinary service links remain useful without JavaScript. The native dialog/mobile sheet has explicit labels, finite icon preview, Save for everyone, Cancel and confirmed Reset name/link/icon. Blank/reset removes only shared name/link/icon, restoring NPM/generic defaults for everyone; category/order and unrelated entries remain. An entry disappears only when no fields remain. An ordinary browser save of legacy metadata serializes the complete preserved document as deterministic v3, including unseen entries. In unreleased source, a v4 input stays v4 losslessly; only explicit icon operations may promote legacy data to v4.

Shared drafts survive harmless polling/search and clear on identity or editing/service-visibility loss. Whole-file/target conflicts keep the draft and disable saving until explicit reload/review, never per-field merge or silent overwrite. Save is announced only after confirmation; other viewers update on ordinary polling/reload. Shared drafts, form tokens and search are memory-only, never browser storage or URL parameters.

The API requires trusted-proxy identity, unique raw identity headers, exact configured login/Host and a currently visible positive ID. POST additionally requires exact Origin, a 30-minute identity/origin-bound HMAC CSRF token, acceptable Fetch Metadata, exact JSON content type and a strict body at most 16 KiB. Missing/invisible IDs are indistinguishable. Responses are no-store/frame-denied with no CORS. Fresh complete authorization is checked immediately before save using the existing three-poll-interval cutoff; this is not transactional upstream-revocation enforcement. Metadata never mutates authorization state.

docs.title: Finite embedded icons
docs.text:
Available IDs are generic, adguard-home, gitea, grafana, home-assistant, immich, jellyfin, nextcloud, nginx-proxy-manager, paperless-ngx, portainer, qbittorrent, and uptime-kuma. Removing a shared icon restores the existing fallback (which may be no image); an empty browser override restores the current server icon, including metadata. In unreleased source, an empty authored personal icon inherits the shared application default, while explicit generic overrides it. Selection is explicit, never inferred from a private hostname. No uploads, arbitrary paths, external icon URLs, favicon fetches or runtime logo-service calls exist.

The twelve unmodified PNGs come from Dashboard Icons revision 57e939e, bounded, decoded and visually reviewed before embedding. assets/service-icons/provenance.json records exact upstream paths, sizes and SHA-256 digests; LICENSE and ATTRIBUTION.txt retain Apache-2.0 attribution. The generic SVG is an original inert project asset. Trademarks remain their owners' property; licensing grants no trademark rights, affiliation or endorsement. Arbitrary logos, access history and account-synchronized personalization remain deferred.

docs.title: Shared storage, conflicts and recovery
docs.text:
One process owns the single file and stable adjacent lifetime lock. Require a regular non-symlink, single-link target owned by the runtime effective UID with owner read/write and no group/other write; its dedicated directory must also be runtime-owned, owner-rwx and not group/other writable. Ancestors cannot be symlinks or non-sticky group/other-writable directories. No chmod/chown/ACL repair occurs. Do not replace/unlink a live lock inode.

Saves use whole-file byte revisions: any intervening edit, even unrelated, conflicts. A separate opaque revision detects changed NPM targets/defaults but ignores poll timestamps. No fingerprint/generation/tombstone is persisted. Positive IDs are not stable identities: review/remove obsolete metadata when deleting/reusing an NPM ID. Reuse can receive old presentation, never new authorization.

A save creates an exclusive adjacent 0600 temporary file, writes and fsyncs, rechecks disk/current visibility/target, renames, fsyncs the directory, then publishes confirmed immutable memory. Known failures before attempting rename preserve the original file. An attempted-rename error or later directory-sync/publication failure is uncertain: all shared writes and authoritative editable read-back are disabled until validated restart/reconciliation. Last confirmed presentation may still render on already-visible cards, but is not proof of disk state. Never claim disk rollback, blindly retry or delete synchronization files.

Live external editing is unsupported while the dashboard writer runs. Drift causes conflict; byte rechecks are not race-proof against uncooperative external writers. Stop the writer, privately merge/review the complete file preserving every field and ownership/mode, then restart. Startup validates/syncs disk before enabling editing, without migration. For uncertain saves, stop, reconcile disk against a reviewed private backup/intended save, then restart with a valid known document.

Before first v3 save, separately approve private backup/restore and compatibility rollback. RC.16 is v1/v2-only: rollback requires compatible metadata and editing-disabled configuration, not image alone. Do not just lower the version with v3 fields retained. Restore a reviewed v1/v2 backup or produce a compatible document privately, reviewing presentation changes. RC.17 already supports v3/shared editing but not the new mode selector; browser localStorage is not sent to that binary or migrated into its file. No production backup/transfer/migration is performed here.

For unchanged non-root/private-port mount alternatives, see TrueNAS shared editing.

docs.title: Shared icons and metadata v4 (RC.20 candidate)
docs.text:
V4 extends the same SERVICE_METADATA_FILE; there is no second shared presentation store. It is readable in off/browser/shared modes only with a valid PORTAL_STATE_NAMESPACE equal to the document's namespace and a control_plane equal to the selected provider. Merely configuring namespace does not enable writing or migrate legacy metadata. It binds the selected control-plane and NPM catalog pair by operator assertion, not a verified upstream UUID or credential.

All six root keys are required; all arrays must exist, even empty. This synthetic minimal document is valid for namespace portal-demo-01 and Tailscale, but do not copy the demonstration namespace as a deployment identity:

{
  "version": 4,
  "namespace": "portal-demo-01",
  "control_plane": "tailscale",
  "services": [],
  "machines": [],
  "applications": []
}
Array / target Stored key and meaning services / NPM Existing positive proxy_host_id; optional existing name/URL/category/order/icon fields. NPM ID reuse can inherit old presentation within a namespace; remove obsolete mappings when repurposing IDs. machines / Machine Exactly device_id_type (id or nodeId), device_id, finite icon. Source-bound typed provider identity, not name/IP. applications / personal destination Exactly target_digest (sha256: plus 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits), finite icon. Server-derived destination key, never an authored personal record ID.

The complete file remains 256 KiB, with 1,024 aggregate entries across all three arrays, not 1,024 each. Unknown/duplicate/case-variant keys, null arrays, duplicate target keys, invalid Unicode/scalars, noncanonical integer forms and excessive nesting (depth 16) are rejected. V4 permits explicitly present NPM name:null/url:null to survive an icon reset even when no other optional field remains; null remains no override. Other fields cannot be null. Headscale v4 requires empty machines and applications and supplies only NPM defaults.

Stable Tailscale presentation IDs use the actual API field provenance, never a guessed type: canonical ASCII string IDs match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,127}; numeric API id accepts only nonnegative canonical decimal integer spelling, preserved as a string. Supported id wins; nodeId is used only for a genuine supported fallback. Ambiguous/unsupported IDs make the shared artwork target unavailable, not an otherwise authorized card invisible. A rename preserves the same typed identity; replacement/reenrollment or a changed ID kind does not inherit icons through a reused hostname/IP. Exact upstream typed-ID reuse cannot be detected as different hardware.

An application digest hashes a versioned length-framed tuple: namespace, tailscale, personal_application, typed device-ID kind/value, https, effective decimal TCP port and exact canonical escaped path. Default port is 443; empty/root path normalizes to /; /app and /app/ remain different. Explicit default :443 remains invalid authored input. Hostname, login and personal record ID are not part of this shared destination key. The shared file contains no raw application URL/path. A digest is not encryption or guaranteed secrecy: plausible paths can be guessed; namespace is not a secret salt. No path-level authorization is implied.

Shared icon tools require the exact editor allowlist and a current visible target. NPM uses the existing matcher; Machines require the full supported SSH + independent Grant TCP/22 + current SSH-enabled/unblocked device projection. Applications require the maintainer's own active entry with fresh direct-member/owner evidence, in RAM or durable mode. No foreign private-record enumeration, reverse digest lookup or matching-user count is exposed. Two owners' active entries to the same destination may intentionally receive the same default without disclosing each other's entries.

Precedence, after visibility matching:

Card Highest to lowest NPM Explicit browser-local override → shared metadata icon → existing fallback (which may be no image) Personal application Explicit authored icon → shared destination default → generic Machine Shared Machine default → existing fallback (which may be no image)

Empty authored personal icon means inherit; explicit generic masks a shared default. Computed defaults never enter authored private records, revisions or browser recovery copies. Shared icon reset removes only that icon/default; ordinary browser NPM reset removes name/link/icon while preserving category/order. Personal blank icon removes only the owner's override. Metadata never creates or authorizes any card.

docs.title: Lossless writers and binding failure
docs.text:
Ordinary browser NPM save/reset keeps legacy→v3 and v4→v4. Only an explicit shared icon set/reset may promote the complete legacy file to v4, under a valid configured binding. Even explicit icon reset can promote. Every writer preserves unrelated arrays, root binding, fields and applicable null presence; no downcast/rebinding or startup rewrite occurs. An icon-only mutation does not clear name/link/category/order. The MCP shared order writer follows the ordinary NPM rule (legacy→v3, v4→v4, v5→v5) and changes only category/order of the named entries.

Configured v4 binding mismatch fails preflight when a readable v4 document is recognized, including off/browser mode; the bound runtime reader also rejects mismatched/invalid reloads without publishing a partial snapshot. Ordinary unreadable/malformed readonly metadata follows complete-refresh failure semantics, not automatic repair or empty fallback. Shared writer startup requires a valid bound document. A valid readonly v4 file does not initialize a lock or writer. Operator hostname proposals remain v1 fragments: merge offline while the writer is stopped, preserving the entire v4 document, never replacing it with a proposal.

docs.title: Custom PNG logos and metadata v5 (unreleased source)
docs.text:
Unreleased source, opt-in, not verified deployment

This is local source only. No published image contains it, and no deployment, live test or native-client run has exercised it. Leave PORTAL_CUSTOM_ICONS absent unless a separately approved compatible image and backup exist.

An authorized shared maintainer can import a small PNG once through MCP, receive a reusable content ID, then assign, read back or clear that ID on a currently visible NPM service card. There is no browser upload control, URL ingestion, network fetch, filesystem path, logo discovery, per-application fingerprinting or SVG. Machines, personal applications and personal cards keep the finite icon behavior. Existing finite icon assignments, including shared icons on every kind, are unchanged.

docs.title: Enablement and authority
docs.text:
Setting Behavior PORTAL_CUSTOM_ICONS absent Off. MCP discovery, tools, rendering and file versions are unchanged. PORTAL_CUSTOM_ICONS=enabled Exact lowercase value only; any other supplied value fails configuration. Also requires PORTAL_EDIT_MODE=shared (or the inferred shared editor), PORTAL_MCP_ORIGIN and PORTAL_STATE_NAMESPACE.

The three tools appear only when enabled and the caller already passes the existing shared-tool capability: trusted-source exact human login on the PORTAL_EDITORS allowlist, exact Host/Origin rules, a held shared writer, a fresh complete snapshot and a valid binding. Every call repeats those checks; import and assignment also repeat them at the final pre-rename check. Non-editors see no tools and receive no catalog. No new route, listener, mount, writable directory, credential or database exists.

docs.title: Import, assignment and rendering
docs.text:
1. custom_icon_import accepts standard padded base64 of one PNG plus the current shared document revision (read it with custom_icon_get or shared_target_get). The encoded string is length-checked before decoding. The PNG header is checked for dimensions before the full decode.
  2. The pixels are decoded, normalized to 8-bit RGBA and re-encoded. No source chunk survives: text, EXIF, ICC, timestamps, palettes and APNG animation (only the first frame is decoded) are discarded. The ID is sha256: plus the SHA-256 of the canonical bytes. Importing the same image again returns the same ID without writing, even with an old revision, so a retry after a lost response is safe. An authorized editor who has the exact image can distinguish an existing image from a new one with a stale revision: only the new import returns a conflict.
  3. Import alone stores an image. It assigns nothing and grants no visibility. custom_icon_set assigns a stored ID to one visible NPM target using document and target CAS; an empty ID clears the assignment. A missing ID fails with invalid_request. Name, link, finite icon, category and order are preserved.
  4. The portal inlines each assigned image as a data:image/png;base64, source only inside markup for a card the viewer is already authorized to see. There is no image URL, so there is nothing to fetch without authorization, and the content ID never appears in markup. A viewer who cannot see the card receives neither bytes nor ID. Changes appear on the next poll without a restart.

In shared mode, a visible NPM card uses its assigned custom PNG before its bundled icon or existing fallback, within the page's image budget. Browser-local editing is a separate deployment mode and does not render custom PNGs. The shared editor dialog's preview still shows the finite icon; its save and reset deliberately keep the custom reference, so legacy dialogs cannot strip it. Use custom_icon_set with an empty ID to clear it.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Limit Value Encoded import argument 10,924 base64 characters, checked before decoding; a maximal import request still fits the unchanged 16 KiB MCP request limit Decoded input 8 KiB Dimensions 1–128 pixels each way Canonical stored image 8 KiB. Re-encoding can be larger than an optimized source; simplify or shrink the image if import returns invalid_request Stored images 64, referenced or not. Enough for a separate image per card for about 45 cards, with headroom Aggregate stored image bytes 384 KiB; exceeding a quota returns capacity without writing Images inlined per portal response 512 KiB of data-URI text; cards beyond the budget deterministically fall back to their finite icon v5 file size 1 MiB in total, and the non-image remainder is still limited to the existing 256 KiB

Other MCP request and response limits are unchanged. Typical small logos (64×64 or smaller, few colors) are a few KiB. Detailed photographs or noisy images usually exceed the per-image limit.

docs.title: Metadata v5 format
docs.text:
V5 is v4 plus one required root array and one optional NPM service field. V4 files are never silently changed: a file becomes v5 only through an explicit custom_icon_import or custom_icon_set write. A legacy v1–v3 file can be promoted directly to v5 the same way, under the configured binding. Once v5, every writer keeps v5. There is no downcast, rebinding or startup rewrite.

{
  "version": 5,
  "namespace": "portal-demo-01",
  "control_plane": "tailscale",
  "services": [{"proxy_host_id": 3, "icon": "grafana", "custom_icon": "sha256:<64 lowercase hex>"}],
  "machines": [],
  "applications": [],
  "custom_icons": [{"id": "sha256:<64 lowercase hex>", "png": "<canonical standard padded base64>"}]
}

custom_icons rows have exactly id and png. The loader requires canonical base64, an ID that matches the bytes, strict canonical chunk structure (IHDR, IDAT, IEND only, 8-bit RGB/RGBA, no interlace, valid CRCs, no trailing bytes), the dimension bounds and a successful decode. Every custom_icon reference must resolve to a stored image, and duplicate IDs are rejected. Any violation rejects the whole document. Startup then fails closed, and a running poller keeps its previous snapshot. Nothing is repaired, pruned or deleted automatically. Headscale v5 supports NPM custom icons, with empty machines and applications.

A v5 file is accepted when the opt-in is off: images then do not render and the tools are absent, but finite fields keep working and writers keep the file as v5. There is no cleanup tool. To remove unreferenced images, stop the writer and edit the file offline, keeping every rule above. The ID is computed by this build's PNG encoder. A different toolchain may produce a different ID for the same source image. Stored IDs remain valid because they are verified against the stored bytes, not recomputed.

docs.title: Backup and downgrade
docs.text: Back up the complete shared file before enabling the opt-in and before the first import. Every older release rejects version 5, including RC.20-candidate source without this feature. Rolling back the image without a compatible document makes the shared metadata unreadable: refreshes keep failing and shared-writer startup fails. Before downgrading, stop the writer and restore a reviewed v4 (or older) backup, or prepare an offline copy without custom_icons and custom_icon fields, set version 4, and remove PORTAL_CUSTOM_ICONS. Never simply edit the version number while keeping v5 fields. Keep the v5 backup for a later return.

docs.title: Durable personal storage (RC.20 candidate)
docs.text:
PORTAL_PERSONAL_SERVICES_FILE is an independent persistence opt-in. Absent retains the existing browser-managed RAM mode, including explicit possibly stale browser restoration after restart. A supplied file requires Tailscale, enabled canonical PORTAL_PERSONAL_SERVICES_ORIGIN, a valid common PORTAL_STATE_NAMESPACE, and a canonical absolute file path (no padding, controls, .., or root path). Missing, corrupt, wrong-bound or unsafe configured private storage fails startup; no RAM fallback occurs. MCP personal read/create/update/delete require durable mode. No new upstream endpoint or OAuth scope is used.

Durable collections bind to namespace + exact trusted login + authoritative Users API user ID/direct-member status, not device owner inference. Every private read, render and mutation requires fresh complete matching owner evidence. Removed/shared/reassigned logins cannot recover an old collection; a renamed login cannot adopt the same user ID automatically. Cold or stale snapshots withhold private content. Once ownership passes, inactive authored destinations remain manageable without active links. Active links still require unique current hostname plus positive ingress TCP Grant evidence; the disk never caches that decision.

docs.title: Private snapshot schema and limits
docs.text:
One whole private snapshot persists only authored data, ownership and store/revision bookkeeping. It has no policy, topology, tokens, sessions or access decisions. A collection record means initialized, including an empty document. Bounds are 128 collections including initialized-empty, 128 entries / 64 KiB canonical authored data per collection, and 9 MiB complete serialized snapshot. GET never allocates and capacity never evicts another owner.

The initial file must already exist. This is a schema-valid synthetic example, not an identity to copy into production:

{
  "version": 1,
  "namespace": "portal-demo-01",
  "store_id": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
  "collections": []
}

The exact root keys are version, namespace, store_id, collections. Version is integer 1; StoreID is 32 lowercase hex characters, stable across ordinary restarts. For a new separately approved empty store only, generate an independent StoreID with python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(16))'; this prints an ID and provisions nothing. Choose and retain a canonical source namespace separately. Never regenerate either on each restart or reset an existing collection to the example.

Each nonempty collections element has exactly login, user_id, revision, document; revision is a positive canonical decimal uint64 string. document is the existing version-1 personal document with authored entries. Logins and user IDs are unique across the snapshot. Unknown/duplicate/case-variant fields, nulls, malformed Unicode, trailing JSON and depth over 16 fail validation. Do not hand-invent ownership IDs or bulk seed private entries: normal admitted creation binds authoritative ownership. There is no new initialization/import CLI or MCP bulk-restore tool.

docs.title: File safety and confirmed saves
docs.text:
The dedicated private directory must be owned by the runtime effective UID, exact mode 0700; the snapshot and any adjacent lock must be regular, single-link, same-owner files, exact mode 0600, without special mode bits. Neither symlinks nor hardlinks are supported. The directory walk uses held descriptors and NOFOLLOW for every component; ancestors must be directories owned by root or runtime UID, no setuid/setgid or group/other write. Only root-owned sticky /tmp or /var/tmp ancestors receive the narrow temporary-directory exception; the dedicated directory itself is always 0700. Container-visible ancestors are validated; host-side storage/ACL safety must also be separately reviewed.

Startup validates the preexisting file before creating its adjacent <filename>.lock, takes a nonblocking exclusive lifetime lock, rereads and syncs the file/lock/directory, and keeps the directory held. It does not initialize a missing snapshot, change ownership/modes or repair storage. A second process cannot share the store. Do not unlink/replace a live lock. Configured metadata/health targets and their .lock paths are excluded from private file/lock collisions, including existing inode aliases; ambiguous path spellings fail rather than changing the exclusion target. Use independent directories and nonoverlapping mount targets, not hardlink aliases.

Each save validates the complete bounded candidate, checks whole-file CAS, writes an exclusive adjacent 0600 temporary file, syncs/closes it, rechecks disk and concrete current ownership/transport authority, attempts adjacent rename, syncs the directory, then publishes confirmed memory. Success is not acknowledged before required sync. A known pre-rename failure leaves the old state; an attempted-rename error or later sync/publication uncertainty suppresses all authoritative private reads and writes in browser and MCP until validated locked reopen/reconciliation. Old RAM must not be used as proof of rollback. Confirmed reads are not external-writer detection; live external writers are unsupported. Shared storage has its own lock/failure domain, not a cross-file transaction.

Fresh process generation is separate from stable StoreID and persisted per-collection revision. All three participate in durable mutation CAS. Owner/request/freshness loss after a confirmed sync may withhold the response without undoing disk. Cancellation, timeout or response loss never justifies replay. Current snapshots may remain usable for up to three polling intervals; polling delay and the final-check-to-rename gap are not transactional upstream revocation. File/directory fsync is not a disaster-recovery or distributed-filesystem guarantee.

docs.title: Browser restart and recovery behavior
docs.text:
After normal restart, healthy durable disk becomes authoritative without Restore from this browser, once a fresh owner snapshot is available. All browsers may be offline during restart. Initialized-empty remains authoritative. Old process CAS fails instead of silently rebasing.

Unsaved drafts and conflicting legacy browser copies remain for explicit review; they are not automatically uploaded or overwritten. Explicit legacy browser restoration is allowed only into an absent collection with current ownership/CAS, not over an initialized-empty or existing durable collection. There is no equivalent MCP import. Missing/corrupt configured disk is a startup failure, not permission to adopt a browser copy.

Browser copies contain validated authored data/bookkeeping (including durable StoreID where applicable), never policy/tokens/access decisions. They are not the authoritative backup of durable storage. An uncertain result must not overwrite recovery copies. Read back confirmed state, compare privately and deliberately resolve conflicts; no auto replay/merge, offline queue, newest-copy guarantee or distributed synchronization is provided. NPM browser choices, logo and SSH-account preferences remain browser-local.

docs.title: Offline backup, restore and downgrade
docs.text:
No backup or provisioning is performed by the application or these docs. Before first durable/v4 write, obtain a separate owner checkpoint recording exact host/container paths, runtime UID/GID, modes and ACLs, private backup location/retention, expected schema/namespace, verified image digest and rollback procedure. Never loosen /mnt/personal/docker-configs/velociportal or its existing 950:950, directory 0750, file 0640 permissions. The private 0700/0600 directory is independently provisioned, not a repair of that protected directory.

  1. Stop the sole writer/deployment before operator edits, backup restoration or source replacement. Keep browser drafts and possible intended-but-unacknowledged changes for private comparison. Do not delete locks under a running process or assume a timeout means no disk change.
  2. Back up complete documents privately, preserving owner, mode, namespace and StoreID, alongside compatible configuration and image records. Protect private URLs/ownership from public logs/repositories; browser copies do not replace this backup. Shared/private files are independent commit domains: record the backup point for each, never claim a cross-file atomic snapshot.
  3. Reconcile actual disk before resuming after uncertainty. Compare the stopped file with reviewed backup/intended change. Restore or retain only a complete validated document at the same approved path/owner/modes. Missing/corrupt/wrong-bound files must be corrected through that explicitly approved offline procedure, not chmod/chown, automatic migration or fallback. Validated locked startup rereads/syncs; fresh owner evidence still gates private access.
  4. Treat backup rollback as possible data loss. It can lower persisted collection revisions or reintroduce old authored rows. Ordinary same-store restore retains its namespace/StoreID; the new process generation rejects old in-flight CAS. Preserve conflicting browser copies/drafts for review instead of automatically importing them or claiming newest recovery. Restore tests belong in a separately approved isolated environment; fsync alone is not backup validation.
  5. Source replacement is not an ordinary restart. Changing tailnet/control-plane source or NPM database requires stop, deliberate namespace rotation and explicit offline mapping reconciliation. Check NPM IDs and typed Machine IDs against the new source; never copy by display name. Namespace-only editing cannot migrate application digests because their preimages are absent: recreate defaults from current authorized owners' entries or omit them in a reviewed replacement. Private login/User-ID reconciliation is a separate reviewed operation, never automatic adoption, account merge or deletion. Do not bypass mismatches by blindly rewriting binding fields.
  6. Prepare compatibility before image downgrade. Older RC.18/19 readers cannot read v4 or provide durable personal/MCP behavior. Use a separately reviewed compatible metadata backup/document, disable editing, remove unsupported MCP/private-file/namespace settings as appropriate for the exact older binary, and preserve the durable private snapshot offline with its compatible configuration. Removing only the file knob deliberately selects volatile mode and does not migrate disk data to RAM. Do not lower a JSON version while retaining new fields, downgrade only the image, delete the private file, or promise lossless recovery through browser storage. RC.16 additionally requires v1/v2 metadata and removal of shared editor settings. Retain the forward-compatible backups and immutable image records before proceeding.

Custom PNG logos add metadata v5, which every older reader rejects. See custom PNG backup and downgrade before rolling back an image that wrote v5.

See the MCP release/live worksheet for pending native-client, genuine identity, browser, restart and permission-removal evidence. Temporary-file tests and static review are not installed-storage recovery acceptance.

docs.title: Tailscale API
docs.text: Velociportal's Tailscale SaaS adapter is OAuth-only and remains labeled preview until live acceptance passes.

docs.title: Fixed production origin
docs.text:
Production code always uses:

https://api.tailscale.com/api/v2

There is no TAILSCALE_API_URL, insecure TLS mode, environment-proxy use, redirect following, or configurable test origin in production configuration. Test-only constructors can point fixtures at local servers.

docs.title: OAuth client credentials
docs.text:
Required environment variables:

CONTROL_PLANE=tailscale
TAILSCALE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=...
TAILSCALE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=...

Velociportal requests an access token from:

POST /oauth/token

with the OAuth client-credentials grant and exactly these scopes:

policy_file:read
devices:posture_attributes:read
devices:core:read
users:read

No API-key fallback, pre-acquired access-token variable, explicit tailnet variable, or credential-derived API origin exists.

Access tokens:

  • remain only in process memory;
  • are shared across concurrent callers;
  • refresh about five minutes before expiry;
  • are replaced once after an API 401; and
  • disappear on restart.

Client IDs, client secrets, rejected access tokens, replacement tokens, and URL-encoded credential forms are redacted from error output. Doctor and validation do not print them.

docs.title: Runtime endpoints
docs.text:
Velociportal uses the OAuth credential's - tailnet alias:

Method Path Purpose GET /tailnet/-/acl Read policy for the selected tailnet GET /tailnet/-/users Resolve exact user IDs, loginName, type, and role; build authoritative per-login Grant-role membership GET /tailnet/-/devices?fields=all Read device IDs, owners, addresses, names, tags, and optional SSH/incoming-connection presentation fields

Each request has an independent timeout. The hardened client requires normal certificate and hostname verification, TLS 1.2 or newer, bounded response headers and bodies, no redirects, and no environment proxy.

docs.title: Policy response
docs.text:
The policy validator reports legacy_acl_visibility_v1 for ACL-only input and network_access_visibility_v1 when accepted Grants participate:

  • legacy acls accept rules remain supported; their destination ports and protocols are not modeled;
  • safe network Grants are additive with ACLs and must carry non-empty src, dst, and ip arrays;
  • Grant capabilities accept wildcard, port/range, protocol wildcard, and protocol port/range forms; card evidence requires TCP to the exact NPM forward_port;
  • exact humans, defined groups, *, and Users-API-authoritative human-role autogroups may become Grant browser card sources;
  • valid tags, IPs, CIDRs, host aliases, autogroup:tagged, autogroup:shared, and other machine selectors may load but never map to a human browser identity;
  • attr-only nodeAttrs accept only *, individual users, defined groups, tags, and autogroup:member targets with the funnel attribute, and never authorize cards;
  • postures, IP sets, services, non-empty via, application capabilities on grants a person can match, malformed capabilities, and unknown semantics fail the refresh; app-only grants and app capabilities on machine-source-only grants are ignored;
  • SSH is not card evidence and is reported separately; and
  • empty policy is a complete zero-card snapshot.

Headscale remains legacy-ACL-only. This Tailscale subset is intentionally narrower than the full policy language, and Tailscale remains the enforcement boundary.

docs.title: User role and device conversion
docs.text:
User loginName is the exact matcher-facing identity because Serve supplies Tailscale-User-Login in that form. The complete Users API response is authoritative for Grant-role membership: a user with type: "member" receives autogroup:member plus autogroup:<role> for owner, admin, member, it-admin, network-admin, billing-admin, or auditor; the duplicate is removed for the member role. The Owner additionally receives autogroup:admin, matching the automatic memberships shown by Tailscale. A user with type: "shared" receives no human Grant-role selectors.

Role membership is consulted only for Grant sources. It requires exact loginName equality and does not case-fold or fall back to local-part, short-login, or bare-login forms. Specialized roles do not imply one another. Membership is never inferred from devices, device ownership, node tags, or tagOwners. Legacy ACLs and nodeAttrs do not consume this mapping.

Velociportal rejects:

  • blank or duplicate user IDs;
  • blank or duplicate login names;
  • missing, null, non-string, blank, padded, or unsupported user type values;
  • missing, null, non-string, blank, padded, or unsupported user role values;
  • an ID that collides ambiguously with another user's login;
  • unresolved or ambiguous device owners;
  • blank or duplicate device IDs; and
  • untagged devices without an owner.

Device owner references may identify a user by API ID or exact login, but that separate mapping must resolve uniquely and is used only to construct node ownership, including supported destination and autogroup:self behavior. It never creates Users API role membership. Tagged devices without a human owner are retained for destination tag resolution. Addresses and tags are trimmed, deduplicated, and sorted.

The full Devices response may also contain sshEnabled and blocksIncomingConnections. Velociportal retains only a sparse true-only device-ID map when both values are exact JSON booleans, SSH is enabled, and incoming connections are not blocked. A machine row now requires its exact ID in this map in addition to supported SSH-policy and Grant TCP/22 evidence. Missing, null, malformed, wrong-type, false, blocked, or mismatched values fail closed and remove the machine instead of offering a command to a phone or another non-SSH device. This is current device self-report that narrows the visibility projection, not posture evaluation, authorization, health, reachability, or proof that SSH will succeed. Doctor consumes only the resulting coarse machine count and never exposes capability values. Other profile and posture data are not retained as snapshot state.

docs.title: RC.20 candidate presentation and durable-owner projections
docs.text:
The current source additionally retains the already-fetched Users API exact login → validated user ID/direct-member mapping for durable personal ownership. Fresh complete evidence must match persisted namespace/login/user ID on every private read/render/write; a reused login or changed ID cannot adopt an old collection. Device-owner mapping remains separate. No new scope or API endpoint is introduced.

Shared Machine/application artwork uses a separate optional typed presentation-ID projection from actual device id versus nodeId provenance. It does not reinterpret the legacy node ID or broaden visibility. Supported canonical IDs persist across rename; replacement or an ID-kind change does not inherit by hostname/IP.
